newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Euro bourses mixed but Frankfurt hits peak.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Euro bourses mixed but Frankfurt hits peak.

text.p: European bourses began business in a mixed mood on Tuesday with Frankfurt hitting a new trading high but others hesitant ahead of U.S. economic data due later in the day.
The dollar strengthened in early transactions as traders took an optimistic view of the outcome of a policy-making meeting of the U.S. central bank and inflation indicators out at 1330 GMT.
German stocks were the star performers. Floor and screen trading both hit intra-day peaks, boosted by the strengthening dollar which was seen as helping exports.

In pre-bourse deals, computerised trading on the IBIS index surged to 2772.29 points as the dollar climbed decisively over the psychologically-important 1.50-mark level. The previous best of 2765.61 was set on Tuesday in a late rally.
Floor trading opened in a similar buoyant mood and the DAX index rapidly advanced to a trading high of 2773.10 points, eclipsing the earlier record set last Friday.
Both indices fell back slightly in later dealings, though the dollar continued to display strength after supportive comments by German central bank officials on Tuesday.
Analysts saw the momentum lessening. "The rally is feeding the rally, but today with somewhat less foaming at the mouth," said one dealer.
Tuesday's late IBIS rally came after comments by Bundesbank council member Edgar Meister that the dollar trading below 1.50 marks was "not appropriate" boosted the U.S. currency.
In London, Europe's biggest bourse, stocks edged lower in nervous trading despite another record close on Wall Street, the fifth in succession.
Activity was muted ahead of the rate-setting U.S. Federal Open Market Committee meeting (1400 GMT).

Most analysts expected the Fed would hold rates steady amid signs that the see-saw U.S. economy was settling down and this would be greeted with relief by global equity markets. New York's current bull run is rooted in this view.
Clues about inflationary pressures in the United States were also possible from U.S. October producer prices due out Wednesday, with October consumer prices and retail sales published on Thursday.
London's shares were further depressed by inflationary worries after a larger-than-expected fall in unemployment was shown in government figures issued on Wednesday.
While leading shares have reclaimed some of the ground lost in recent weeks, traders said further advances were likely to be limited until the UK budget, on November 26, was out of the way.
In Paris, stocks slipped 0.5 percent at the opening following a year high struck on Tuesday. A large state sale of shares in Elf adding to consolidation pressure.
On currency markets, the dollar strengthened against the mark and the yen, buoyed up by traders optimism over the FOMC meeting.

"You almost have this Goldilocks scenario in the U.S. with solid sustainable growth and no inflation. Certainly in the near term I don't see that threatened," said Stuart Weatherby, economist at Panmure Gordon.
Analysts said the U.S. currency was also supported by comments on Tuesday from Bundesbank officials, including Bundesbank President Hans Tietmeyer, supporting a firmer dollar.
Tietmeyer said the dollar was again on its way up back up and that he always welcomed the dollar at its correct level.

"German industrial production figures have been weaker than expected. In light of that, the Buba is not going to want a strong Deutsche mark...I wouldn't rule out further cuts in repo rates further out," said Weatherby.
CURRENCIES AT 1020 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5070 marks and 111.45 yen, compared with 1.5015 marks and 111.38 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1020 GMT
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares was 7.6 points lower at 3,926.7.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 38.01 points at 2,772.31.
PARIS - The CAC 40 index was down 10.04 points at 2219.09
PRECIOUS METALS AT 1020 GMT
Gold was quoted at $382.75, up from $381.75 at the London close.
